name: CA-23
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans nine points Republican and the Republican incumbent is running
Obernolte holds roughly $1.4 million to Hodge's $17,000 in cash on hand
Prediction markets price Obernolte's re-election at 97 percent
No polls, expert ratings, or meaningful outside spending against the incumbent
model.rationale: The Republican incumbent runs in a district that leaned nine points Republican, backed by a roughly fifteen-to-one cash advantage and negligible outside opposition. Markets price his re-election at 97 percent, and no polling or spending signals suggest a contest.
model.watch: A late wave of Democratic outside spending or a surprise surge in challenger fundraising would be the first sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 23rd District leans nine points Republican, and Republican Jay Obernolte is seeking re-election as its incumbent. He has raised about $1.8 million and enters the final stretch with roughly $1.4 million on hand, while Democrat Tessa Lynn Hodge has raised about $123,000 with under $20,000 available. Outside groups have spent modestly to support the incumbent and almost nothing against him.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give the Democrat about a one percent chance of winning. The fundamentals point the same way: the district's partisan lean, the incumbency advantage, and the fundraising gap all favor Obernolte, and the national political environment would need to swing dramatically to put the seat in play. The forecast treats this as a safe Republican hold.
